key_insight: Graph neural networks can screen dissociative water adsorption on nickel using only bare-metal geometries, without constructing or relaxing adsorbates during screening.
engineering_relevance: This approach reduces the cost of identifying favorable OH*+H* configurations on nickel nanoparticles relevant to heterogeneous and electrochemical catalysis.
method: Define candidate O- and H-binding sites using sets of nickel anchor atoms.
Build adsorbate-free graphs from anchors and their local environments in MACE-relaxed bare nickel structures.
Use separate GNNs to predict adsorption energies and whether proposed binding sites survive DFT relaxation.
evidence_signal: The energy model achieved 0.031 eV internal-validation MAE; independent tests covered unseen Ni55, Ni91, Ni130 clusters and larger surface cells, with particularly promising relative-energy ranking.
watch_item: Quantitative accuracy varies across systems, so deployment should validate energy predictions and retention filtering on representative target structures.
paper_title: Adsorbate-Free Screening of Dissociative Water Adsorption on Nickel Nanoparticles via Graph Neural Networks
